cards.text: Picture it, friend. Paul, the apostle, just got dragged out of the temple by a mob, chained up by the commander of the Roman regiment, and CARRIED up the steps by soldiers. Right at the door of the barracks, he turns to the commander and asks, 'May I say something to you?'

cards.question: Paul's in chains and still asking to talk. What does the Roman commander ask him right back?

cards.text: Then the commander asks if Paul is somebody else entirely. You ever wave BIG at someone across a parking lot, and it is NOT who you thought?

cards.question: Who does the commander ask if Paul is?

answers.text: The Egyptian who led a rebellion
Judas the Galilean who led a revolt
Theudas who gathered four hundred men

cards.text: And this Egyptian led four thousand members of the Assassins into the wilderness. Friend, in that junk drawer I got mistaken for a bottle opener, a paperweight and a doorstop, but NEVER for the leader of four thousand Assassins!

cards.question: Paul sets the commander straight: 'I am a Jew from ___ in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city.'
Then Paul asks the commander to let him speak to the people.

cards.text: Permission granted. Paul stands on the steps and motions to the crowd, the SAME crowd that just wanted him gone.

cards.question: When Paul motions to the crowd from the steps, a great hush comes over them.
Paul spoke Greek with the Roman commander, but he addresses the crowd in ___.

cards.text: Paul starts his defense right there on the steps: 'Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense before you.' BROTHERS and FATHERS, friend, to the same crowd that just wanted him gone!

cards.question: When the crowd hears Paul speaking to them in Hebrew, they get even more quiet.

cards.text: Paul tells them he's a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia but raised right here in Jerusalem. He's showing his ID at the door before anybody even asks for it.

cards.question: Paul says he was educated in strict conformity to the law of their fathers. At whose feet did he learn?

cards.text: Paul says he was as zealous for God as any of them, and he persecuted this Way, the followers of Jesus, even to the death. He's not hiding his record, friend, he's reading it OUT LOUD, and he says the high priest and the whole Council can testify to it.
He even got letters from them to bring believers in Damascus back to Jerusalem to be punished. So there he is, about noon, almost to Damascus, and SUDDENLY...

cards.question: Paul is on his way to Damascus at noon. What suddenly flashes around him?

answers.text: A great wind from the sea
A pillar of fire from above

cards.text: Paul falls to the ground and hears a voice: 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?' Saul is Paul's other name, and when somebody says your name TWICE, friend, you stop whatever you're doing.

cards.question: Paul asks the voice on the Damascus road, 'Who are You, Lord?' Who answers him?

cards.text: Paul asks, 'What should I do, Lord?' Jesus tells him to get up and go into Damascus, where he'll be told all that he's been appointed to do.

cards.question: After that brilliant light, Paul walks into Damascus on his own, seeing just fine.

cards.text: In Damascus there's a man named Ananias, a devout observer of the law, highly regarded by all the Jews living there. Ananias comes and stands right beside Paul.

cards.question: Ananias says, 'Brother Saul,' and at that moment Paul gets his ___ back.

cards.text: Then Ananias says the God of their fathers has appointed Paul to know His will, to see the Righteous One and to hear His voice. The man who was hunting believers just got a WHOLE new job description.

cards.question: Ananias tells Paul he will be His ___ to everyone of what he has seen and heard.
Ananias tells Paul to take his time and think it over before he gets baptized.

cards.text: Later, back in Jerusalem, Paul is praying at the temple and falls into a trance. He sees the Lord saying to him, 'Hurry! Leave Jerusalem quickly, because the people here will not accept your testimony about Me.'
Paul answers, 'Lord, they know very well that in one synagogue after another I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You.' Friend, I can't even win an argument with my oven timer.

cards.question: Paul keeps reminding the Lord of his past. What does he say about Stephen, the Lord's witness?

answers.text: He watched over the garments of his killers
He tried to stop the crowd that killed him
He buried him outside the city walls

cards.question: Then the Lord tells Paul, 'Go! I will send you far away to the ___.'

cards.text: The crowd listens to Paul right up until that last line about the Gentiles. Then the volume comes BACK.

cards.question: The crowd stops listening when Paul says the Lord sent him to the Gentiles. What do they shout about Paul?

answers.text: That he is not fit to live
That he should go back to Tarsus
That he should be set free

cards.text: They're shouting, throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air. Friend, I've seen some upset bakers, but I have NEVER seen anybody throw their apron AND the flour.

cards.question: With the crowd this wild, the commander has Paul brought into the barracks. What does he order next?

answers.text: That Paul be flogged and questioned
That Paul be released at once
That Paul be sent to the high priest

cards.question: The commander wants to find out the reason the crowd is shouting against Paul.

cards.text: The soldiers stretch Paul out to strap him down. And right then, Paul turns to the centurion standing there, a Roman officer, with a question. Oh, this is about to get GOOD.

cards.question: Paul asks the centurion, 'Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman ___ without a trial?'

cards.text: The centurion goes straight to the commander: 'What are you going to do? This man is a Roman citizen.' That's the face you make when you honk at the car in front of you, and it pulls into the parking spot marked BOSS.

cards.question: The commander goes to Paul and asks if he's a Roman citizen, and Paul says yes.

cards.text: Then the commander says, 'I paid a high price for my citizenship.' I bet he's ready to compare receipts.

cards.question: The commander paid a high price to become a Roman citizen. How did Paul become one?

answers.text: He paid an even higher price

cards.question: The men about to interrogate Paul step back at once, and the commander is ___ when he realizes he put a Roman citizen in chains.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave Paul for now. Trust me, friend, the oven timer on this story has NOT gone off yet.

findings.problem: The card tells events from the previous passage without their references. It cites only Acts 21:37, but Paul being dragged out of the temple, chained by the commander and carried by soldiers comes from Acts 21:30-35.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Are you from Rome' is close to what the commander actually asks Paul later in the passage: 'are you a Roman citizen?' (Acts 22:27). A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new event in Papa Dorin's backstory: being mistaken in the junk drawer for a bottle opener, a paperweight and a doorstop. Invented moments are only allowed around his bakery.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to fill in a word ('Tarsus') from a line of Paul's that they haven't seen. Nothing earlier lets them reason it out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Half of the stop's six choice cards are pure discovery with no setup to reason from: the commander's Greek question (card 2), the Egyptian (card 4) and Tarsus (card 6). Card 3 says only that the commander thinks Paul is 'somebody else entirely,' which gives no context for card 4.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: 'The SAME crowd that just wanted him gone' draws on Acts 21:36 ('Away with him!'), which is in the previous passage. The card cites only Acts 21:40 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'The same crowd that just wanted him gone' again draws on Acts 21:36, outside the passage, with no reference. It also repeats the line from stop 1 card 8.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card carries three beats: Paul's zeal, his persecuting the Way to the death, and the high priest and Council testifying.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: 'Saul is Paul's other name' is a fact from outside the passage (Acts 13:9), and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Acts 22:9 is never told: Paul's companions saw the light but could not understand the voice. This is an important detail of the Damascus road account, and the stop skips from verse 8 to verse 10.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the soldiers strapping Paul down, Paul turning to the centurion, and 'Oh, this is about to get GOOD.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line nearly copies the doc's example: 'And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.' The card's first sentence and 'Trust me, friend' are lifted almost word for word.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
